scope: Google/Gmail sign-in and email-code password recovery
status: Implemented; Google OAuth and Gmail delivery await owner credentials
googleSetup: Create an OAuth client of type Web application in your Google Cloud project. Configure consent and test users if the application is in Testing.

Register the exact redirect URI http://localhost:3000/api/v1/auth/google/callback for local APP_URL=http://localhost:3000. For Production, use https://<your-domain>/api/v1/auth/google/callback and matching APP_URL.
Put GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID and GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET in the ignored .env file on the server; never NEXT_PUBLIC_, source code, browser storage, logs or chat.
Restart the existing API process. /api/v1/auth/google/config will report enabled only when the required configuration is present. Validate real sign-in manually after configuring the Google client.
Existing Milo customers sign in with their password first, then choose Tài khoản → Bảo mật, reauthenticate and link Google with the same email. No automatic email merge.
New Google accounts have USER role. To enable password reauthentication or unlink their last Google login method, create a local password using the email-code recovery flow first.
gmailSetup: Use the shop-owned Gmail sender account with Google 2-Step Verification enabled. Create a Google App Password if the account supports it; use this instead of the normal Gmail password.

Set SMTP_USER to the complete sender Gmail address and SMTP_PASSWORD to its App Password without grouping spaces. Set EMAIL_PROVIDER=smtp only when credentials are ready. SMTP_HOST=smtp.gmail.com, SMTP_PORT=465, SMTP_SECURE=true are already prepared locally.
Restart the existing API and worker once. Keep only one running application stack. Email sending needs the worker, Redis and database.
Google sign-in credentials and Gmail SMTP credentials are separate. A customer signing in with Google does not grant Milo access to their mailbox.
Run an owner-controlled delivery check after configuring SMTP; check Inbox/Spam and Outbox job status. No external email was sent by this implementation session.

Gmail imposes delivery/sending limits. Failed delivery retries the existing email outbox; it does not switch to another provider or purchase services. Expired, replaced, verified or consumed recovery codes are skipped.

security.emailCode: Six digits; 10 minutes; five wrong attempts; replacement invalidates previous code
security.resetProof: Random 256-bit, hashed at rest, one use, at most 5 minutes within original code expiry
security.mfa: Retained during reset and required during Google login when enabled
security.sessions: JWT/session revocation unchanged; all revoked after recovery
security.oauth: Authorization code + PKCE S256 + state bound to HttpOnly browser cookie + nonce; SDK verifies ID token; stable provider subject; pending login in HttpOnly cookie; no provider tokens retained
security.storage: Email-code HMAC at rest; email text encrypted in outbox; only development file mail contains readable code inside ignored .local/mail
security.business: Existing cart, payment, order, inventory and seller workflows preserved
security.logging: Callback returns no-store and no-referrer; default Next development incoming logging and Nginx access logging exclude OAuth callback credentials. Temporary OAuth and MFA setup entries are excluded from Admin settings.

deployment: Install lockfile dependencies, run Prisma generate, build API/worker/web and execute the documented tests in isolated databases.
For another deployment, back up and restore-test its database before running prisma migrate deploy. Migration 202611230012_google_recovery adds two tables and does not rewrite existing business data.
Local migration was explicitly approved and applied after backup and clone rehearsal. migration-applied.json records unchanged fingerprints for all 42 original tables.
Production uses HTTPS and matching APP_URL, trusted reverse proxy, private no-store auth responses and the existing production provider/DB role checks.

The provided Compose file is a development stack (NODE_ENV=development). Its mail overrides now respect .env; configure Production separately using existing runtime checks. Do not run the development seed command against Production.

Rollback application code without dropping the additive authentication tables. For data recovery, restore the backup into a fresh database first and inspect before switching connections. Do not delete current shop data.
Configure query-string redaction for OAuth callback credentials in any additional hosting, reverse-proxy, monitoring or error logs outside these application settings.
limitations: No Google Client ID/Secret or Gmail sender/App Password was supplied; live Google consent, token exchange and real SMTP delivery were not verified.
No real Google/Gmail, payment, shipping, Cloudinary or OpenAI requests were performed by the tests. Google provider and browser API responses were synthetic.
SMTP delivery can be delayed or rejected independently of website request success; the request response acknowledges queueing rather than guaranteeing receipt.
Code recovery changes the password, not the email address or active MFA. Losing both the second factor and backup codes still requires a separately verified support process.
